target_customer: Consumers with large personal music libraries who wanted web access to them
problem: People kept music on one computer and could not play it from the web or share it with friends. Anywhere.fm let users upload a library and play it anywhere.
business_model: Free consumer web player, planned revenue from affiliate sales and audio ads
product_category: Consumer web music locker and player with social features

founders.name: Sachin Rekhi
founders.background_notes: Later founded Notejoy. Calls Anywhere.FM his first startup; says Paul Graham rejected the first idea but let them in if they found a new one.

founders.name: Anson Tsai
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch and InformationWeek coverage of the deal.

competitors.name: MP3tunes
competitors.what: Online music locker with unlimited storage and streaming

competitors.name: Streampad
competitors.what: Web player for a home library, nearly identical product with less polish per TechCrunch

competitors.name: imeem
competitors.traction_then: Over 20 million monthly uniques and 65,000 new registrations a day by its own figures in early 2008

competitors.name: Ezmo
competitors.what: Clone that pulled from iTunes, Windows Media Player and Winamp, sharing capped at ten friends

technical_complexity.rationale: Large uploads, an iTunes style web player and streaming at scale in 2007 were standard engineering with some hard parts. TechCrunch reported no cap on uploaded songs.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch itself noted Streampad was nearly identical, and Ezmo cloned the idea within months. Music licensing was unresolved, so the product had no structural protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: imeem bought the company in 2008-01. imeem itself closed in 2009 after MySpace bought only its domain, technology and trademarks.

market_need_then: Users had large local music libraries and no easy way to reach them from other computers. A cluster of locker and web player products appeared in 2005 to 2007, which shows real interest but also a crowded field.

branding.domain_note: Used anywhere.fm, a .fm domain, which fit the music theme. The domain later redirected to an unrelated site.

identity.visual_style: iTunes look alike web player per YC page

branding.brand_signature: Friend Radio, the feature for streaming friends' playlists
branding.community_and_virality: A blogger posted that he missed the service in 2009; otherwise no fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive name that says what it does, noticed by TechCrunch at launch, but the brand ended inside imeem within months.

outcome_analysis: Anywhere.fm launched in August 2007 with a web player for personal music libraries and reached about 60,000 users and 9 million uploaded songs before imeem acquired it in January 2008 for an undisclosed price. The founders joined imeem for an earnout. The company spent under $100,000, so it was a cheap and quick exit, though terms are unknown and imeem itself shut in 2009.
notes: Funding: TechCrunch says under $100,000 from YC and angels; CB Insights says $20K over 2 rounds; one low quality site says $125K. No discrete round amounts are reliable, so rounds is empty and coverage is marked complete on the basis of the TechCrunch statement. Acquisition date: 2008-01-28 per TechCrunch and PitchBook, 2008-01-22 per CB Insights; Rekhi's own post says end of 2007. Price undisclosed. A low quality site claims Myspace acquired it, which conflicts with all other sources. Technical background of founders not sourced.
